basis.governing_question: How should Atlas Logistics design and pilot a digital freight-matching platform for small shippers in Iberia?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Define the freight-matching platform blueprint and the pilot plan for small shippers in Iberia.

gate.label: Go/no-go on pilot
gate.decision: Is the blueprint approved and the pilot cleared to launch?

phases.name: Pilot
phases.objective_one_line: Launch a first version to a limited group of small shippers and track progress toward 200 active shippers.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Does the steering group accept the pilot results and the scale-up plan?

workstreams.name: Blueprint hypotheses
workstreams.answers: What must hold true about each component of the platform for small Iberian shippers to adopt it?
activities: Frame the blueprint components of the platform
Write testable hypotheses for each blueprint component
Align on scope and hypotheses with key stakeholders

workstreams.name: Shipper and market evidence
workstreams.answers: How do small shippers in Iberia buy freight today, and does the evidence support each hypothesis?
activities: Interview small shippers on how they arrange freight
Analyze market data and documents on Iberian freight demand
Test each hypothesis against the evidence gathered

workstreams.name: Platform prototype
workstreams.answers: What should a small shipper see and do on the platform to get freight matched?
activities: Draft wireframes of the shipper journey
Build a clickable wireframe prototype
Test the prototype with small shippers

workstreams.name: Blueprint and pilot plan
workstreams.answers: What blueprint, tested against the hypotheses, and what plan for the pilot go to the go/no-go decision?
activities: Assemble the blueprint from the tested hypotheses
Define pilot scope, milestones and launch criteria
Review the plan with the CEO, CTO and Head of Sales

workstreams.name: Pilot KPIs and enablement
workstreams.answers: What KPIs, internal roles and stakeholder agreements does the pilot need to track progress toward 200 active shippers?
activities: Agree pilot KPIs with the CEO, CTO and Head of Sales
Identify the internal hires the pilot needs
Report pilot KPI progress to the stakeholders

workstreams.name: First shipper group
workstreams.answers: Which group of small shippers should the pilot launch to first?
activities: Analyze shipper segments using the Design phase evidence
Interview small shippers on whether they would join
Select the first target group for launch

workstreams.name: Platform build and pilot
workstreams.answers: Can the first version be built, launched to the first shipper group and reach 200 active shippers?
activities: Build the first version and prepare it for launch
Launch to the first group, then onboard more shippers
Collect usage data and shipper feedback during the pilot

workstreams.name: Scale-up business case
workstreams.answers: What business case, implementation plan and roadmap does the pilot evidence support for scaling the platform?
activities: Analyze pilot usage data against the 200-shipper target
Build the business case and implementation plan
Draft the roadmap with the CEO, CTO and Head of Sales

deliverables.name: Shipper and market evidence on each hypothesis
Wireframe prototype of the shipper journey
Pilot plan with milestones and launch criteria
Pilot KPIs agreed with key stakeholders
List of key internal hires for the pilot
First target group of small shippers for launch
First platform version with launch record
First-wave pilot usage data and shipper feedback
Scale-up business case with implementation plan and roadmap

events.label: Kick-off
events.decision: Are the scope, team and calendar confirmed for the engagement?
agenda: Present the objective, the two phases and the 26-week plan
Align on scope and the 200-shipper pilot success measure
Confirm the team and the steering meeting calendar

events.label: Workshop 1: first findings
events.purpose: Review first evidence and the prototype
events.decision: Which hypotheses should the blueprint and pilot plan detail?
agenda: Present the hypotheses and the shipper and market evidence
Review the wireframe prototype of the shipper journey
Discuss which hypotheses to detail in the blueprint

events.label: Go/no-go on pilot
events.purpose: Decide on the blueprint and pilot launch
events.decision: Is the blueprint approved and the pilot cleared to launch?
agenda: Present the blueprint with tested hypotheses
Review the pilot plan with milestones and launch criteria
Decide whether the blueprint is approved and the pilot cleared

events.label: Workshop 2: pilot readiness
events.decision: Are the pilot KPIs, hire list and first shipper group ready for go-live?
agenda: Present the pilot KPIs agreed with key stakeholders
Review the first shipper group and the list of key internal hires
Confirm readiness against the launch criteria of the pilot plan

events.label: Workshop 3: first-wave data
events.purpose: Review first-wave data and plan next steps
events.decision: Confirm the first-wave findings as input to the scale-up business case?
agenda: Review the first platform version with its launch record
Present first-wave usage data and shipper feedback
Discuss what the findings imply for the scale-up business case

events.label: Final readout
events.purpose: Decide on the pilot results and scale-up
events.decision: Does the steering group accept the pilot results and the scale-up plan?
agenda: Present pilot results against the 200-shipper target
Review the scale-up business case, implementation plan and roadmap
Decide whether to accept the pilot results and the scale-up plan

architect_notes: Engagement type is assumed from the pilot mention; confirm assessment and implementation before quoting, as it decides whether Pilot is in scope.
Design 8 and Pilot 18 weeks fill the stated 26; the split is an estimate, with Pilot longest so 200 active shippers can build up.
No Implementation or Measurement phase: the platform is new, so Pilot is the last phase and the rollout after it is not in these phases.
